_comment: Project-shape profiles: the single source of truth for which workflows
each profile switches off. Read by cli/slopstopper/profiles.py (the CLI)
AND by install.sh (via python3, resolved from the source checkout), so
there is exactly one copy of this mapping in the project.
A profile only ever SUBTRACTS workflows. `workflows.disabled` in
.slopstopper.yml adds to a profile's set; `workflows.enabled` removes
from it, so an adopter can keep an individual check the profile drops.
Adding a profile: add an entry here, then follow the AGENTS.md row for

ui.summary: A web UI: a site or app that serves HTML to a browser.
ui.detail: Every browser, SEO, security and hygiene check applies. This is the default when `profile:` is unset. The four API checks (api-health, api-headers, api-latency, openapi drift) are added only when the repo has an API: an OpenAPI/Swagger spec or proto file, a server-framework dependency, or one of the API checks configured (api.health.path, api.latency.paths, api.headers.paths or api.openapi.spec). A site with no API doesn't run four jobs that check nothing; configure `api.*` (or list them under workflows.enabled) and re-run the installer to add them.

api.summary: An HTTP API: JSON/gRPC endpoints with no browser-rendered surface.
api.detail: Drops the nine browser-and-SEO checks: they assume HTML, a DOM and a public web surface, so on an API repo they fail rather than no-op. Keeps the four API checks (api-health, api-headers, api-latency, openapi drift) and CSP exceptions (APIs still set response headers; inert until you set headers.source). All of them skip until configured. The Snyk checks (sast, dependencies, iac, sbom) and secrets apply to every profile.

library.summary: A library, CLI or package with no deployed surface of any kind.
library.detail: Drops everything that needs a URL: the nine browser-and-SEO checks, CSP exceptions, and the four API checks. hygiene:openapi is dropped here too, because it is the one hygiene check that needs a live API: drift means the spec against the thing it documents. What remains is the static-analysis layer (the Snyk checks, secrets, complexity and the docs checks), which is the whole of what applies to code that nothing serves.
